n8a3107b7649.s: In which year was the Treaty of Paris, the last of the treaties of the Anglo-French struggle in the Carnatic, concluded?
n8a3107b7649.x: The Treaty of Paris was concluded in 1763, after Aix-la-Chapelle (1748) and Pondicherry (1754).

n3f0490933bb.s: Which of the following battle–year pairs is NOT correct?
n3f0490933bb.x: Wandiwash was fought in 1760, not 1764; 1764 is the year of Buxar.

n5e1bd21f8b7.s: Under the Dual Government in Bengal, criticised as "power without responsibility", the Nawab formally retained the:
n5e1bd21f8b7.x: The Company enjoyed the financial power of the Diwani, while the Nawab formally retained the Nizamat and its responsibilities.

new.s: The Third Carnatic War was concluded by the Treaty of:
new.x: The Third Carnatic War (1756–63) ended with the Treaty of Paris (1763). Yandabo closed the First Anglo-Burmese War.

new.s: Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: First Carnatic War – Treaty of Aix-la-Chapelle
Second Carnatic War – Treaty of Yandabo
Third Carnatic War – Treaty of Paris
First Carnatic War – War of Austrian Succession
new.x: The Second Carnatic War ended with the Treaty of Pondicherry (1754); Yandabo (1826) ended the First Anglo-Burmese War.

new.s: The Third Carnatic War was an extension of which European conflict?
new.x: The Third Carnatic War (1756–63) was an extension of the Seven Years' War (1756–63).

new.s: In the Hyderabad succession dispute after Nizam-ul-Mulk's death, the French backed his grandson:
new.x: The French backed Muzaffar Jang, the grandson; the English backed Nasir Jang, the son. Chanda Sahib was the French candidate in the Carnatic.

new.s: After the Battle of Ambur, Muzaffar Jang became the Subedar of the Deccan and rewarded with grants:
new.x: Dupleix backed Muzaffar Jang; after Ambur he became Subedar of the Deccan and rewarded the French with grants.

new.s: Who replaced Dupleix and made peace with the English in 1754?
new.x: Godeheu replaced the recalled Dupleix and made the Treaty of Pondicherry.

new.s: Which English commander, along with Clive, besieged Tiruchirappalli in the Second Carnatic War, forcing the French commander Law to surrender?
new.x: Stringer Lawrence with Clive besieged Tiruchirappalli, where the French commander Law surrendered.

new.s: Count de Lally surrendered Pondicherry to the English on:
new.x: Lally surrendered Pondicherry on 16 January 1761; 22 January 1760 is the date of Wandiwash.

new.s: In which battle of 1749 was Nawab Anwaruddin of the Carnatic killed?
new.x: At Ambur (August 1749), the French with Muzaffar Jang and Chanda Sahib won, and Anwaruddin was killed.

new.s: Robert Clive held Arcot in 1751 with about 210 men for how many days?
new.x: Clive held Arcot for 53 days (23 September–14 November 1751) with about 210 men.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about the Anglo-French rivalry:
1. The English East India Company was a private body run for profit.
2. The French East India Company was state-controlled.
3. The resources of Bengal after Plassey paid for the English wars in the south.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: All three are true: the English company was private, the French state-controlled, and Bengal's resources after 1757 funded the southern wars.

new.s: Bussy won the Northern Circars for the French in:
new.x: Bussy won the Northern Circars for the French in 1753; they were lost after Chendurthi (1758) and the fall of Machilipatnam (1759).

new.s: The French second factory at Masulipatnam (1669) was set up on a patent from the:
new.x: Masulipatnam was the second French factory (1669), set up on a patent from the Sultan of Golconda.

new.s: After the Battle of Tumnapalem (1756), Bussy concluded the Treaty of Charmahal with:
new.x: Bussy won at Tumnapalem with Vijayaramaraju of Vizianagaram, which led to the Treaty of Charmahal.

new.s: Who called the Battle of Chendurthi the "Plassey of Andhra"?
new.x: Malleson called Chendurthi (1758) the "Plassey of Andhra" as it drove the French out of the Northern Circars.

new.s: Pondicherry was officially renamed Puducherry in:
new.x: Pondicherry was renamed Puducherry in 2006, not 1987; it became a UT by the 14th Amendment (1962).

new.s: Which of the following former French settlements is in Tamil Nadu?
new.x: Karaikal is in Tamil Nadu; Yanam is in the Godavari delta of AP, Mahe in Kerala and Chandernagore in Bengal.

new.s: Before becoming Nawab of Bengal, Alivardi Khan was the Deputy Governor of:
new.x: Alivardi Khan was earlier Deputy Governor of Bihar; he took the throne by killing Sarfaraz Khan at Giria (1740).

new.s: Sarfaraz Khan, Nawab of Bengal, was the son of:
new.x: Sarfaraz was the son of Shuja-ud-din (and grandson of Murshid Quli Khan), not Murshid Quli's son.

new.s: Murshid Quli Khan shifted the capital of Bengal from:
new.x: Murshid Quli Khan moved the capital from Dacca to Murshidabad, not the reverse.

new.s: Contract-based revenue collection in Bengal under Murshid Quli Khan, also called ijaradari, was known as:
new.x: Ijaradari, revenue farming through ijaradars, was also called mal jasmani.

new.s: Which fugitive was given shelter by the English in Calcutta, angering Siraj-ud-Daula?
new.x: The English protected the runaway Krishna Das, one of the causes of conflict with Siraj.

new.s: When Siraj-ud-Daula ordered the European companies to stop fortifying their settlements:
o: both the English and the French obeyed
the French obeyed but the English did not
the English obeyed but the French did not
new.x: The French obeyed the order to stop fortification, while the English went on fortifying Fort William.

new.s: In January 1757, Calcutta was recaptured from Siraj-ud-Daula by Clive and:
new.x: Clive and Admiral Watson, coming from Madras, retook Calcutta in January 1757.

new.s: When Calcutta fell in June 1756, Governor Drake fled to:
new.x: Governor Drake fled to Fulta and Holwell surrendered when Calcutta fell in June 1756.

new.s: The Black Hole episode took place on:
new.x: The Black Hole episode took place on 20 June 1756; Plassey was fought on 23 June 1757.

new.s: According to the usual account, how many English prisoners were put into the Black Hole cell?
new.x: 146 prisoners were put into the cell; about 120 died (Holwell's own figure was 123).

new.s: The Battle of Plassey was fought on the banks of the river:
new.x: Plassey (Palashi) lies on the Bhagirathi in West Bengal, about 150 km north of Calcutta.

new.s: Which of the following fought for Siraj-ud-Daula at Plassey and was not part of the conspiracy?
new.x: Mir Madan fought for Siraj; Rai Durlabh, Mir Jafar and Yar Lutuf Khan were in the plot.

new.s: Who called Robert Clive a "heaven-born general"?
new.x: William Pitt the Elder called Clive a "heaven-born general".

new.s: Who is called the "Founder of the British Empire in India"?
new.x: Robert Clive is called the Founder of the British Empire in India (APPSC 2019).

new.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Mir Jafar – Last independent Nawab of Bengal
new.x: Jagat Seth was called the "World banker"; Siraj was the last independent Nawab, Mir Jafar the puppet, and Rai Durlabh the Diwan.

new.s: Under the farman of 1717, the Company could trade in Bengal without customs duties for a fixed annual payment of:
new.x: Farrukhsiyar's farman let the Company trade duty-free in Bengal for a fixed Rs 3,000 a year.

new.s: The farman of 1717 granting the Company duty-free trade in Bengal was issued by:
new.x: The 1717 farman, the "Magna Carta" of the Company, was issued by Farrukhsiyar.

new.s: After Plassey, Mir Jafar paid the Company a sum of:
new.x: Mir Jafar paid Rs 1.77 crore and gave the Company the zamindari of the 24 Parganas.

new.s: Under Najm-ud-Daula (1765), defence and administration were handed to the Naib Subahdar:
new.x: The 1765 arrangement handed defence and administration to the Naib Subahdar Muhammad Reza Khan; the Nawab kept the Nizamat in name only.

new.s: Before becoming Nawab, Mir Qasim was the Fauzdar of:
new.x: Mir Qasim, son-in-law of Mir Jafar, was earlier Fauzdar of Purnia and Rangpur.

new.s: Under the Treaty of Allahabad (1765), Shah Alam II received:
new.x: Shah Alam II got Kora and Allahabad and lived under Company protection; Shuja got his other dominions back.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about the Treaty of Allahabad (1765):
1. It was signed by Clive for the Company.
2. Awadh became a buffer state.
3. The Nawab of Bengal lost the Nizamat.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: Clive signed the treaty and Awadh became a buffer state; the Nawab of Bengal kept the Nizamat, so 3 is wrong.

new.s: Who was the first Mughal ruler to become a pensioner of the Company?
new.x: Shah Alam II, under Company protection at Allahabad after 1765, became the first Mughal pensioner of the Company.

new.s: Under the Dual Government, the naib diwan who collected revenue for the Company in Bihar was:
new.x: Raja Shitab Rai was naib diwan of Bihar; Muhammad Reza Khan served for Bengal.

new.s: Robert Clive's two governorships of Bengal were:
new.x: Clive was Governor of Bengal in 1758–60 and 1765–67.

new.s: Which military reform of Clive took effect from 1766?
o: Stopping the tribute to Shah Alam
new.x: Clive banned double batta from 1766; the tribute to Shah Alam was stopped by Warren Hastings.

new.s: The Bengal famine of 1770 occurred during the governorship of:
new.x: The 1770 Bengal famine came in John Cartier's time, under the Dual Government.

new.s: Which of the following was NOT an ally against the English at Buxar?
new.x: Mir Jafar was the Nawab of Bengal on the English side at Buxar; Mir Qasim, Shuja and Shah Alam II were the allies.

new.s: The Plassey battlefield lies in which district of West Bengal?
new.x: Palashi, on the Bhagirathi, is in Nadia district, West Bengal.
